subject: Tax Overrides and Fire Station Debt Exclusion
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed City Councilor George Scarpelli regarding upcoming ballot questions for a fire station debt exclusion and two Proposition 2.5 overrides. Scarpelli argued against the tax increases, citing lack of transparency, available city reserves, and missed revenue opportunities from new development.

items.title: Overview of Ballot Questions 6, 7, and 8
items.summary: Councilor George Scarpelli explained that Question 6 seeks a $30 million debt exclusion for a fire station, while Questions 7 and 8 request a combined $7.5 million in permanent tax overrides for school operations and programming.

items.title: Opposition to Fire Station Debt Exclusion
items.summary: Scarpelli stated that the firefighters' union does not support Question 6 because they were excluded from the final design process for the proposed headquarters.

items.title: Impact of Permanent Tax Overrides
items.summary: Scarpelli distinguished between temporary debt exclusions and permanent Proposition 2.5 overrides, which he noted compound annually and remain on tax bills indefinitely.

items.title: Criticism of Tax Calculator and Assessments
items.summary: Scarpelli claimed the city assessor's office was not involved in creating public tax calculators and warned that 2025 property reassessments will likely cause further tax increases.

items.title: Financial Task Force Transparency Concerns
items.summary: Scarpelli criticized the lack of public minutes or participation from the administration’s financial task force prior to the override proposal.

items.title: Free Cash Funding Alternative
items.summary: Scarpelli detailed his rejected proposal to use $5 million of the city's $24 million in 'free cash' to fund schools instead of seeking a tax override.

items.title: Economic Development and New Growth
items.summary: Scarpelli argued that the city has failed to generate revenue from new development, citing several blocked 40B housing projects that would have provided significant permit fees and tax base growth.

items.title: State Audit and Official Pay Raises
items.summary: Scarpelli noted that the City Council voted down his request for a state audit and approved pay raises for elected officials despite the administration's claims of a financial crisis.
